compiled_kernel_resources.scope: Static compiler declarations, not measured occupancy.

implementation: Replace the absolute-product zero-C WMMA with eight-byte L2-norm and maximum metadata per operand row/block. Eligible original BF16 squares are exact in F64; sequential positive sums, square root and final F32 conversion use the existing20-ppm outward allowance. Unsupported blocks return infinity. The product of outward norms bounds the absolute dot by Cauchy-Schwarz; maximum products bound every individual BF16 product. Groups8/16/32/64 correspond to K128/256/512/1024, reducing scalar envelope evaluations. Each signed K16 matrix product still uses zero C and explicit FP32 addition. Track maximum rounded partial and entry-center-plus-partial magnitudes. Charge every scalar addition against one ULP of the observed partial barrier, add conditional native2^-19 error, and solve the observed-prefix fixed-point envelope for all21 original alignment/normalization units per K16. Grouping changes center additions, which remain inside the new interval. All ambiguous endpoints replay the complete original staged2 arithmetic. No runtime dispatcher changes.
correctness_scope: Sanitized host tests enumerate all65536 BF16 encodings in three row contexts, test independent wide canonical arithmetic under three modeled native errors for widths1024/4096, and check every block norm/product bound, original interior carry, endpoint interval and sampled suffix. The native route uses complete replay only. GPU generated cases include width16, odd K16 tails80/272, cancellation, signed zero, unsupported rows, and widths through8192. Every captured BF16 output is compared with GB10, selected raw FP32 values with original canonical GPU replay, and sampled complete dots with independent CPU wide sums. Metadata bounds, full prepared words, candidate permutations, guards and unused capacity are checked; separate audits verify metadata byte immutability and production selection parity. References are comparison inputs only. Finite tests do not prove the conditional native coefficient universally. Repeated CPU and encoding counts are deduplicated.
timing_scope: Original C64/full replay and four macro norm/full replay variants. One warmup and three measured completed host samples rotate whole-operator order. Include original lossless row preparation, eligibility, complete norm metadata generation, producer, selection, count read and all selected replay. Allocation, clearing, canonical/CPU reference computation, validation and separate audits are outside clocks. All variants preallocate maximum metadata capacity. This measures an operator owner, not production allocation ownership, startup or TTFT. The captured q8192 operands repeat1023 rows from q7169 and are not a real-model token loop. The QKV C64 control is slower than the retained QKV matrix producer.

decision.reason: All numerical, guard and metadata checks pass, but the best macro route regresses complete OUT by27.3332ms and C64 QKV by29.8919ms. Larger blocks regress further despite fewer matrix operations and envelope evaluations. Do not infer gains from operation counts or candidate counts. Separate the metadata and producer stages before choosing the next structural implementation; the current per-thread metadata scan has strided neighboring-lane loads.
decision.next_measured_question: Determine the completed preparation and producer costs, and evaluate coalesced block metadata preparation while preserving conservative norm/max bounds and complete original replay.
